newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees plywood prices on upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees plywood prices on upward trend.

text.p: Indonesia's timber industry sees international plywood prices continuing on an upward trend following high demand from the key Japanese market, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Friday.

"Prices for Indonesian plywood are likely to continue moving up following high demand from Japan," Indonesia Wood Panel Association (Apkindo) executive director Tjipto Wignyoprajitno was quoted as saying.
"Japan remains the main market for Indonesian plywood and Japan often becomes a benchmark for the international plywood price," he added.
Wignyoprajitno said export prices in June were $507.3 per cubic metre, up from April's $449.6.
He said high plywood demand, especially for use as panels for concrete construction, followed the start of the construction season in Japan.
"Demand for concrete panels rose 45 percent in the second quarter compared with the first quarter this year," he added.
Apkindo, which has a monopoly on Indonesian plywood exports, said total exports to 13 countries in June reached 554,058 cubic metres. Indonesia exported 8.5 million cubic metres of plywood in 1995.
